upcoming.title: Glitter Trashcan Productions: A LEWDicrous Masquerade
upcoming.body:
Hide & Cheek: A LEWDicrous Masquerade

Who are you when nobody knows it's you?

On September 25, Glitter Trashcan Productions invites you to a burlesque, drag and variety show where every performer is hiding... something... while revealing everything else!

Behind every mask lurks a secret... a glamorous stranger? A seductive beast? A mysterious hero? An absolute gremlin? This isn't your average masquerade ball -- it's LEWDicrous! Expect elaborate helmets, animal faces, safety equipment, full-face disguises, impossible creatures, and the bizarre fever dream you just can't get anywhere else.

Whether you're drawn to elegance, absurdity, or simply enjoy watching beautiful weirdos take their clothes off while wearing increasingly wild and wacky headwear, Hide & Cheek has you covered.

Performances by:
Sophie du Mal
Amber Dextrous
Kit Katastrophic
Anna Nymph & Essie Hex
Temera Titty
Aiden Antares
Vida Catastrophe D'Ho
Blasphemy
Divina Moorephina
Viva Vendetta

Hosted by the fabulous Kisa Von Teasa

Doors at 7:00 PM

Show at 8:00 PM

Venue is fully accessible. ASL interpretation will be present.

LEWDicrous is funded in part by the Regional Arts & Culture Council and the Office of Arts & Culture

Tickets at TreeTix.com

upcoming.title: Feng E-Taiwanese Uke Sensation
upcoming.body:
Feng E’s only Portland Show!

Advance tickets $20 here, $25 day of show, all ages

Feng E first stunned the world at just ten years old when his mesmerizing ukulele rendition of Tommy Emmanuel’s Classical Gas went viral. Almost overnight, the young prodigy became an international sensation—appearing twice on The Ellen DeGeneres Show and captivating millions more on Asia’s Got Talent and America’s Got Talent.

With nearly one million YouTube subscribers and countless millions of views, Feng E continues to push boundaries and redefine what the ukulele can do. In 2025, he  and his band Resonance Effect captured the top prize at Taiwan’s Taoyuan Iron Rose Hot Sound Awards—their version of Idol.

Now, this teenage virtuoso returns to U.S. stages, ready to captivate audiences once again. Experience the energy, emotion, and pure joy of an artist who’s redefining a generation of music.

upcoming.title: KC Craine & Tin Compass Record Release!
upcoming.body:
KC Craine and Tin Compass - Record Release!

purchase tickets here

Tickets $20 in advance, day of show $25, all ages, doors open at 6:30pm

KC Craine and Tin Compass return to Hoku Events for a special album release concert celebrating their new album, “It’s Not The Destination.”

This will be a special evening of new, all-original music from Portland songwriter, guitarist and producer KC Craine. A distinctive songwriting force in the Portland music scene, KC brings heartfelt storytelling and soulful melodies to songs rooted in the Pacific Northwest and shaped by folk, country, Zydeco and soul.

Tin Compass is difficult to put in a box. Accordion, violin, mandolin, bass, percussion and harmony vocals create a rich and unexpected sound that moves well beyond the usual folk and Americana formula. The result is soulful, distinctive and refreshingly original music with a warm, organic groove.

Come experience KC Craine and Tin Compass.

upcoming.title: Portland Blues & Jazz Dance Society Tuesday Blues!
upcoming.body:
PB&J Dance Society presents dancing to Live Music from Karen Maria & Jonah Bradbury

Please register and pay on the Portland Blues & Jazz Dance Society website or at the door

$20 sliding scale

7:00 - Lesson - an hour lesson for all levels!

8:00 - Live Music - Karen Maria & Jonah Bradbury

10:00 - DJ 

What is Tuesday Blues?

Tuesday Blues is an all-ages, weekly social partner dance event in Portland established in 2003, and is open to people of all dance backgrounds and experience. It offers both beginner and intermediate lessons before each of our weekly dances. We strive to have an inclusive environment at all our dances, where we can grow dancers into community members. Every Tuesday night we bring you the best Blues dancing, DJs, and live music Portland has to offer.

There's no partner required, no experience required—just a love for the blues and a desire to move!

Full bar and snack available! Fully ADA accessible. Paid parking in front, plenty of street parking to north and west.

upcoming.title: HOKU Comedy Night!  Andrew Sleighter
upcoming.body:
D&D Comedy presents Comedian Andrew Sleighter!

See Andrew's new 1-hour comedy special on Thursday before it is taped on Saturday.


ANDREW SLEIGHTER started in comedy looking for the perfect funny line to open a biography. Since then, Andrew’s laid-back style and clever writing have won him appreciation from fans and respect from his peers.

Andrew performed on Last Comic Standing, recorded a comedy special for Dry Bar, and made his late-night stand-up debut on Conan. He's also written and performed sketch comedy for Comedy Central and written and blogged for the Sports Show with Norm Macdonald on Comedy Central. Most recently, Andrew appeared on The Late Late Show with James Corden.

Don't miss Andrew's new 1-hour special two nights before he films it.

upcoming.title: Alexandr Misko, Forest Bailey
upcoming.body:
Advance tickets $25 here, $30 day of show

all ages, doors open at 6:30pm

Alexandr Misko

This international guitar sensation brings his groundbreaking stage show to the USA for the very first time! Hailed as “the future of guitar”, Misko is a globally renowned virtuoso known for his jaw-dropping technique, emotional depth, and genre-defying style.

 Fusing classical precision with elements of jazz, rock, and modern fingerstyle, his performances are both technically astonishing and deeply moving. Misko’s self-taught, boundary-pushing approach has captivated millions online, earning him a massive global following and praise from some of the world’s top music publications.

 What the Press Says:

•    “Misko is the future of guitar.” - Total Guitar Magazine

•    “A one-of-a-kind performance that will leave you speechless.” - The Guardian

•    “Alexandr Misko redefines guitar playing with every note he plays.” - MusicRadar

•    “A mesmerizing display of technical brilliance and raw emotion.” - Rolling Stone

•    “A true guitar prodigy.” - Guitar World

•    “An artist who combines virtuosic technique with deep musical expression.” - Guitar Player Magazine

 Tickets are VERY limited for these intimate concerts — don’t miss out!

Opener Forest Bailey crafts a unique combination of fingerstyle, tapping and percussive playing that is all his own. Drawing from various influences like Michael Hedges, Andy Mckee, Antoine Dufour, Scale The Summit, Led Zeppelin, Chon, and Covet, each song is a musical journey that further shows what two hands and a guitar can accomplish. He underscores these sonic adventures with an exciting, welcoming and humorous stage presence that exudes every ounce of passion he has for his craft.

upcoming.title: Kivett Bednar Band & The Andy Moore Blues Band
upcoming.body:
Advance tickets $15 HERE, all ages, doors open at 6:30pm

The Kivett Bednar Band delivers a powerful, modern take on the blues, combining deep roots, soulful musicianship, and high-energy performances. Frontman Kivett Bednar grew up in Austin, Texas, surrounded by the sounds of one of America’s great blues and roots music cities. He discovered the blues through his father’s record collection, developing an early appreciation for the guitarists, singers, and songwriters who shaped the tradition. After moving to Portland, Oregon, in 2012, Kivett became part of the Pacific Northwest blues community and developed his own distinctive voice as a guitarist, singer, and songwriter.

The Kivett Bednar Band was named Best New Act at the 2024 Muddy Awards and Best Contemporary Blues Act in 2026. The band also won the 2026 Journey to Memphis and will represent the Cascade Blues Association at the 2027 International Blues Challenge in Memphis, Tennessee.

The lineup features Oregon native and Berklee College of Music graduate Jeff Langston on bass; 2026 Muddy Award Best Drummer winner Edwin Coleman III; and Pat McDougall on organ and keys, a multi-award-winning artist and songwriter who performs with some of Portland’s most prominent acts.

Andy Moore is a Portland , Oregon based blues singer and harmonica player. 

Originally from Tennessee, Andy is a veteran performer of both Memphis’ Beale Street , Lower Broadway in Nashville, and clubs across the South. 

Andy has appeared on stage and performed with blues and roots artists such as Rattle Snake Mama, Justin Townes Earle , North Mississippi All Stars, Kivett Bednar Band, Curtis Salgado, Chris Daniels & The Kings, Mitch Kashmar, and many more. 

“..you’re blowing good harp and thats truth”

Steve Freund- James Cotton Band Guitarist 

“Good Licks, Good Vibrato , Good Everything”

Hank Shreve -Hohner Harmonica Endorsee

upcoming.title: Jon Koonce & the Gas Hogs Reunion
upcoming.body:
Advance tickets $25 at afton tickets, $30 Day of show

Doors at 6pm, all ages, seated show!

Jon Koonce is a Portland treasure from his days in the 70s playing in Portland bands such as Sleazy Pieces in legendary clubs like La Bamba, Euphoria, Last Hurrah and Sak’s Front Avenue. He left the drum throne and went on to fronting his own band, Johnny & The Distractions, and getting signed to A&M Records based on his success in the Northwest. The band toured the country opening for arena shows for Asia, J. Geils Band, and Tom Petty. This was followed by a solo album, also on A&M.

Jon is bringing a treasure trove of Vinyl (2017), CD’s and books for purchase.

The band for this special performance is: Andy Gauthier, Scott Portzline, Evan Shlaes, Denny Bixby

upcoming.title: The Too Loose Cajun/Zydeco Band
upcoming.body:
Advance Tickets $20 HERE, Day of Show $25

Doors open at 1:30pm, all ages

Too Loose Cajun/Zydeco Band

If you’ve never heard French Louisiana-style dance hall music, you’re in for a real treat. And if you have, welcome back y’all!

For more than twenty years, the Portland-based Too Loose Cajun/Zydeco Band has been playing their infectious brand of dance music from Southwestern Louisiana — at festivals large and small, parties, street fairs, and weddings throughout the Pacific Northwest.

Take a great electric band, add two fiddles, an accordion, and a traditional rub-board, and you have an irresistible sound: happy, exciting, and exceptionally rhythmic. You won’t be able to sit still, guaranteed.

Their repertoire includes Cajun, Zydeco, and New Orleans-influenced music, with male and female vocals (and harmonies), and lyrics sung in English and Cajun French. For you dancers, there are two-steps, a few waltzes, and a surprise or two.

So come on down (and bring your dancin' shoes).

Sean Daly & The Shams - Irish Rebel rock

The Shams are an eclectic crew — folk, punk, rock, and tradition colliding into something that hits different every time. From intimate pub nights to headlining the American Music Hall, they bring the full weight of that history to every note.

Lead by Sean Daly who grew up in Donegal, he listened as The Wolfe Tones sang songs about Ireland, and The Irish Brigade sang songs about the ten. At thirteen, he stood in front of more than a thousand comrades and sang "Joe MacManus" — and something locked into place.

He carried those songs with him across the ocean, through San Francisco bars and rock and roll stages, even when the setlists said otherwise. The longing to sing songs of freedom never left him. When he brought his family back to Donegal, he found his way back to those songs too.

Check out their sound at: www.seandalyandtheshams.com

Opening act Vince & Kacey will bringtheir heartfelt and clever lyrics, with a style influenced by John Prine, Jason Isbell, and Bruce Springsteen.

21+ show - Doors at 7:30  Show at 8pm.

Full bar and Hawaiian Bowls available.

Tickets at Afton

past.body:

doors open at 6pm, all ages

Sprig of That is a tabla, fiddle, cello, and guitar quartet playing a hearty Midwest-raised and globally inspired acoustic stew. Pushed by producer Jayme Stone, the band stakes new sonic terrain for itself on Foragers, their upcoming full-length featuring guest appearances by Sierra Hull, Olov Johansson (Väsen), Simon Chrisman, Rohith Jayaraman, and Wes Corbett (who produced their 2023 release bloom).

Formed in Minneapolis, MN in 2018, the group has played legendary venues from Portland’s Old Church Minneapolis’ Cedar Cultural Center and NYC’s Rockwood Music Hall; warmed up stages for artists like Chris Eldridge/Kristen Andriessen, the Andrew Marlin String Band, and Charlie Parr; performed at festivals like Pickathon and Blue Ox; and collaborated with organizations like Carnegie Hall and Minnesota Public Radio to give educational workshops across the country.

past.title: Dave Fleschner & Friends (live Blues)
past.body:
A Rare Night Home: Dave Fleschner & Friends

Two Sets at Hōkū Events on Madison, tickets $15

Thursday September 10 · 7:00 PM ·

1125 SE Madison St, Portland, OR

Featuring Alan Hager, Dan Gildea, Bill Athens and Edwin Coleman III

Dave Fleschner is currently on tour with blues legend Tommy Castro and the Painkillers, which makes Portland shows a rare occasion these days. On May 21, he’s home for one night at Hōkū Events — two sets of American roots music with an all-star lineup.

You might know Alan Hager — the reigning Cascade Blues Association Muddy Award winner for Electric Guitar — as the longtime guitarist with Curtis Salgado. But before Alan hit the road with Curtis, he and Dave had a duo residency at O’Connor’s Vault, where they recorded The Hager Fleschner Duo – Live From The Vault (available at davefleschner.com). Alan also appears on Dave’s The Blues Cabaret. This show is a rare chance to hear that partnership back in action.

Also on guitar is Dave’s good friend and longtime collaborator Dan Gildea — a Portland jazz mainstay who has played with Ron Carter, Leroy Vinnegar, and Shelly Rudolph. Dan has played on a number of Dave’s records, including The Dave Fleschner Trio – Deep Cuts, At Home, and The Blues Cabaret. Two guitar masters whose very different styles lock in beautifully together.

Joining the fun on Bass this time around is Bill Athens. Long time performing and recording collaborator with Dave, you have also heard Bill playing either upright or electric with Sleater-Kinney, 3 Leg Torso, Trio Subtonic, the Rose City Chamber Orchestra, the Tacoma Symphony, Seamus Blake, Dave Pietro, Bel Canto Northwest, Dan Balmer, Mel Brown, George Colligan, Nancy King, Tom Grant and many more.

Anchoring the whole thing is Edwin Coleman III, this year’s CBA Muddy Award winner for Drummer of The Year and a longtime cornerstone of Portland’s best bandleaders — equally at home in a Hammond jazz trio, a blues revue, or a soul band.

The setlist will move through selections from the recent vinyl release The Dave Fleschner Trio – Deep Cuts, along with material from The Blues Cabaret and Live From The Vault, plus a handful of vintage blues classics and Bob Dylan favorites.

past.title: John Nilsen and SWIMFISH
past.body:
Tickets in advance $15-$25 or day of show $20-$30 at afton tickets

Doors open at 6pm, all ages

John Nilsen was inducted into the Oregon Music Hall of Fame in October, 2024.

It’s sometimes surprising when a band writes some of its own material. SWIMFISH is a colorful band featuring high quality, original folk/rock music. 

The line up is bass, drums, guitar, piano, mandolin, harmonica & vocals, but their focus lies in first class songwriting. Of course they play some covertunes, but they are full time musicians/recording artists who also compose great music and Yamaha Piano Artist/band leader John Nilsen’s one million plus record sales warrant it.

SWIMFISH has a unique sound. Singer/songwriter originality based on cultural experience separates them. 

The debut CD by SWIMFISH, John Nilsen & SWIMFISH, was played throughout the USA on radio to positive reviews. 

Late founding member of the major rock band, AMERICA, Dan Peek, wrote, “ Major kudos on your CD. The music is superb,

the lyrics inspired and the production/arranging are top notch. The songwriting hangs together well and the tracks flow, carving out a groove like a river carves a canyon. You deserve to be heard.” 

The Oregonian says, “John Nilsen’s

career is the envy of many musicians.” John Nilsen &

SWIMFISH released, The Future of the Past, their 5th CD in Jan. 2026.

Consisting of John Nilsen - guitar, piano, vocals / DonWoodward - guitar, mandolin, harmonica, vocals / Mike Snyder - drums, percussion / Dave Captein - bass / Bob Logue - guitar, vocals, SWIMFISH came into existence as John Nilsenʼs guitar and vocal band when taking a break

from his demanding international piano career. Don

Woodward was the first SWIMFISH member to sign on as the two had grown up as next door neighbors and taught each other to play guitar as teenagers. Mike Snyder, who has played with many of the finest musicians in the NW and had been on numerous John Nilsen recording sessions joined the band when it was formed in 2006. Oregon Music Hall of Fame bassist Dave Captein joined the band for their

2nd album. Guitarist & vocalist, Bob Logue, a longstanding veteran guitarist/vocalist of the NW music scene, also joined the band for their 2nd album. 

John Nilsen and SWIMFISH are finding their groove again with all new material. That comes as no surprise.

www.johnnilsen www.magicwing.com
